environment.description: Same Spring Boot service deployed behind CloudFront distribution d1234abcdef.cloudfront.net with origin access restricted via custom origin header validation. The CloudFront distribution is configured with a cache behavior that adds a custom header 'X-Origin-Verify: a9f3c7e2-81d4-4b6a-bc3f-7e2190d5f4a1' to all origin requests. The ALB has a listener rule that returns HTTP 403 for any request missing this header with the exact value. Additionally, the CloudFront distribution has a Viewer Request function (CloudFront Functions runtime) that enforces path-based access: requests matching /api/v1/media/sessions* require a valid CloudFront signed cookie with key-pair-id K2JCJMDEHXQW7F (separate from the content signing key-pair). The signed cookie policy restricts access to the /api/v1/media/sign path only. The CloudFront Functions code validates that the cookie's custom policy JSON does not include the /sessions path pattern. Origin requests to /api/v1/media/sessions* that arrive without the X-CF-Authorized: true header (set only by the viewer request function upon successful cookie validation) are dropped by a second ALB rule with priority 1.

config.alb_rule_priority_1: IF path=/api/v1/media/sessions* AND header X-CF-Authorized != true THEN fixed-response 403
config.alb_rule_priority_2: IF header X-Origin-Verify != a9f3c7e2-81d4-4b6a-bc3f-7e2190d5f4a1 THEN fixed-response 403
config.cloudfront_function: viewer-request function validates signed cookie, only sets X-CF-Authorized:true for paths matching /api/v1/media/sign
config.direct_origin_access: blocked by security group - ALB only accepts traffic from CloudFront managed prefix list (com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing)
config.security_group_ingress: pl-3b927c52 (CloudFront origin-facing IPs) on port 443 only
